role: SessionRecoveryCoordinator extension for recovering sessions from the app's own on-disk/iCloud backups, the trash, the H10's internal recording (workout/overnight augment, interrupted-workout auto-recovery), paused-state restore, and the one-time merge-data-loss repair migration; plus file-scope helpers and the InterruptedWorkoutAutoRecovery in-flight registry.
types: SessionRecoveryCoordinator: extension — backup/trash/strap recovery and merge repair
SessionRecoveryCoordinator.WatchRouteRecoveryResult: enum — recovered/distanceOnly/noRoute/failed outcome of Apple Health route recovery
SessionRecoveryCoordinator.StrapAugmentResult: enum — merged/notConnected/noStrapData/failed for workout strap merge
SessionRecoveryCoordinator.MergeDamage: struct — which merge-repair conditions a linked child session has
InterruptedWorkoutAutoRecovery: enum — lock-protected static set of session ids currently being auto-recovered at launch
state: ud:reviewedRecoveredWorkoutIds (static let reviewedRecoveredKey, string array capped at 50, :423)
ud:autoRecoverAttempts_<sessionUUID> (per-session int attempt counter, :519, removed only on successful auto-recovery)
toplevel: Declares the three result enums and MergeDamage struct inside the extension; file-scope private helpers unrecoveredBackupIds/newestWorkoutBackup/recordAutoRecoveryAttempt; InterruptedWorkoutAutoRecovery enum with a static lock initialised to an empty set (:837).

flags.text: SessionRecoveryCoordinator.pullCloudBackupsToLocal (:33) is only reached through RRCollector.pullCloudBackupsToLocal (RRCollector+RecoveryForwarding.swift:30), which has no caller in the repo; SessionRecoveryService calls its own pullCloudBackupsToLocal internally (SessionRecoveryService.swift:175).

units.does: Lists lost sessions (backups with no archive entry) via SessionRecoveryService.checkForLostSessions, excluding ids of recordings currently live (liveRecordingIds) so an in-progress night is not offered for deletion.

Builds the set of session ids that are live right now: the collector's current session when isCollecting, its paused session, and the WorkoutRecorder's current session when it is recording or finalizing.

branches.cond: collector.isCollecting and currentSession has an id
branches.effect: current session id inserted; otherwise skipped
paused session id inserted; otherwise skipped

branches.cond: a WorkoutRecorder exists, its phase is .recording or .finalizing and it has a currentSession
branches.effect: recorder session id inserted; otherwise skipped

flags.text: isCollecting is mirrored from polarManager.isRecordingOnDevice by bindRecordingStateTracking, so any running strap recording (even an orphan from a crash) marks collector.currentSession as live when one is set.

units.does: Pass-through to SessionRecoveryService.pullCloudBackupsToLocal (downloads iCloud live backups into local RawRRBackup).

flags.text: Only caller is RRCollector.pullCloudBackupsToLocal (RRCollector+RecoveryForwarding.swift:30), which nothing in the app or tests calls.

units.does: Pass-through to SessionRecoveryService.checkForDeletedSessions: the trash list (deleted ids with backups) as (id,date,beatCount).

Restores a trashed session: un-marks it deleted (and tells iCloud trashRestore), puts back the trashed file if the trash kept it, else rebuilds from the raw backup; on rebuild failure tells the iCloud trash-restore tracker to abandon.

branches.cond: restoreKeptSession returned a session (trash kept the file and re-archive succeeded)
branches.effect: returns it immediately; otherwise falls through to raw-backup rebuild
restoreFromTrashFailed abandons the iCloud restore; the unmark-deleted from line 42 is NOT rolled back, so the id is no longer marked deleted while nothing was restored; returns nil either way

flags.text: SessionRecoveryService.restoreFromTrash swallows a failed unmarkAsDeleted (logs only) and this function proceeds; archive.archive then throws sessionWasDeleted inside restoreKeptSession/recoverFromBackup and the user just sees restore fail with no reason.

units.does: Puts a trashed session's kept file back: loads it from the trash, links/supersedes any same-night session recorded since, archives it with skipSameNightMerge, discards the trash copy, marks its raw backup archived, force-reuploads to iCloud and bumps the archive signal.

branches.effect: continues; nil → returns nil (caller falls back to raw-backup rebuild)
logs error and returns nil (trash copy kept); caller then tries raw-backup rebuild

units.does: Pass-through to SessionRecoveryService.permanentlyDelete: drop trash copy, raw backup, iCloud live backup and the deleted-id record.
Pass-through to SessionRecoveryService.deleteLostSessions: marks each id deleted in the archive (errors logged).

Recovers a session from its on-disk backup: workout backups (WorkoutTrackBackup header present) go through recoverWorkoutFromBackup; others through the HRV path, bumping the archive signal when the result is complete.

branches.cond: a WorkoutTrackBackup exists for the id
branches.effect: routes to recoverWorkoutFromBackup and returns its result; otherwise HRV path
notifies archive signal on main; nil result skips. SessionRecoveryService.recoverFromBackup only returns complete sessions, so non-nil always notifies

units.does: Runs SessionRecoveryService.recoverFromBackup with closures for windowed/full analysis (collector.analyze), same-night supersede, and enriched recovery scoring; returns the archived recovered session or nil.
calls: closure:analyze/analyzeWithCapacity/supersedeSameNight/computeRecoveryScore closures built here and invoked by SessionRecoveryService

units.does: Ensures the analysis result carries a training context (fetching a fresh one relative to the session's end/start if nil), then computes the composite recovery score via MorningSessionPipeline.

branches.cond: enriched result exists with nil trainingContext AND a fresh context could be created
branches.effect: attaches the fresh context; otherwise result passed unchanged (nil analysisResult stays nil, so `enriched?.trainingContext =` is a no-op)
uses session.startDate as the reference date for the training context

units.does: Rebuilds a crashed workout via WorkoutRecoveryService.recover (reason .appCrashed), feeding it the strap's on-device recording when obtainable; on success bumps archive signal and sets the review/trim card on MorningCoordination.

branches.effect: returns nil with no review card; otherwise publishes and returns outcome.session

units.does: Downloads the H10's internal recording made since the workout's start (stopping it if running) and places it on the workout clock; nil means the recovery service uses the disk backup only.

branches.cond: workout track backup has a header start date AND the strap recording does not belong to a live session
branches.effect: continues; otherwise returns nil (disk backup only)

branches.cond: reconnect succeeds, strap is recording or holds a stored exercise, a recording since workoutStart downloads, and it has points
branches.effect: returns points on the workout clock; otherwise logs and returns nil

flags.text: The live-session guard reads collector.isCollecting, which bindRecordingStateTracking sets to polarManager.isRecordingOnDevice. A crashed workout's strap recording that is still running therefore makes strapRecordingBelongsToLiveSession true, and the H10 pull this function exists for is skipped; launch auto-recovery even requires isRecordingOnDevice==true (strapReadyForAutoRecovery) before calling here, then archives a disk-only (truncated) workout and clears the crash flag.

units.does: Review/trim card Save: clips the archived workout's RR series at endSec and re-finalizes it through WorkoutRecoveryService (discarding backups); with <30 beats left it keeps the workout untrimmed. Either way marks the session reviewed and clears the review card.

branches.cond: archived session or its rrSeries missing
branches.effect: `?? []` → clipped empty → <30 → treated as too-short, marked reviewed, nothing changed
re-finalizes; otherwise marks reviewed, clears card, returns
notifies archive signal; on nil (failed re-finalize) still marks reviewed and clears the card

flags.text: When WorkoutRecoveryService.recover fails, the user's trim is not applied but the session is marked reviewed and the card dismissed with no error, so the over-long workout stays and the card never returns for it.

units.does: Review card Discard: deletes the archived recovered workout (failure logged via attempt), bumps archive signal, marks it reviewed and clears the card; raw backup kept.

flags.text: A failed delete is only logged by attempt(); the card is dismissed and the session marked reviewed, so the rejected workout stays visible with no feedback (the comment at :206-209 acknowledges this).

units.does: Recovers a crash-shortened workout's route/distance from Apple Health: first a Watch workout GPS route (>=2 points) re-finalized through WorkoutRecoveryService; else HealthKit passive walking/running distance if it beats the recorded distance by >50 m.

branches.cond: HealthKit route exists with >=2 locations AND recoverWorkout with that track succeeds
branches.effect: notifies and returns .recovered; otherwise falls to passive distance

branches.cond: hkDistance > recorded distance (nil→0) + 50 m AND recoverWorkout with that distance succeeds
branches.effect: rewrites; otherwise returns .noRoute (also when the rewrite itself failed)

flags.text: A WorkoutRecoveryService failure on the distance-only rewrite returns .noRoute, so the UI reports 'no route' instead of a failure; .failed is only returned when the archive lacks the session.

units.does: Calls WorkoutRecoveryService.recover with the given RR points and either an override GPS track (discarding backups) or an override distance.

'Recover session' for an archived workout: with the strap connected, downloads its recording of this session, merges it with the archived RR (SessionRecoveryMath.mergedWorkoutPoints), re-finalizes with auto-trim and returns duration/beat count.

branches.effect: beat count falls back to merged.count

flags.text: pullStrapRecording refuses whenever strapRecordingBelongsToLiveSession, which is true whenever the strap reports isRecordingOnDevice (mirrored into collector.isCollecting), so a recording still running on the strap is never merged and the user gets .noStrapData.

units.does: 'Pull from strap & re-merge' for an overnight scored from the stream: unless already device/composite-sourced, reconnects, downloads the strap's recording of this night, merges via DataSourceSelector (device preferred), persists the merged series + provenance, then re-scores through reanalyzeSession.

branches.effect: returns .noStrapData (also when refused because the strap's recording is considered live, see pullStrapRecording)
existing = [] and strap points alone go to the selector

branches.cond: merge points nil (selector chose nothing useful) or archiving the merged session failed

units.does: Chooses the points to persist: the selector's points when it returned any (nil if empty), otherwise the strap's when they outnumber the archived stream, else nil.

branches.effect: returns them, or nil when that array is empty; selection nil → next rule
returns strapRR; otherwise nil (no merge reported)

units.does: Re-scores the merged overnight via collector.reanalyzeSession (which reloads from disk and re-archives), bumps the archive signal and returns .merged with source, beat count and recovery score.

branches.effect: uses the persisted-but-unrescored session for the result (score may be the old stream score)

flags.text: A failed reanalysis still returns .merged with the pre-merge recoveryScore, so the UI reports a successful re-merge whose score was not recomputed.

units.does: Begins a strap transfer (BLE hold) and reconnects for it; returns whether the reconnect succeeded.

Downloads the strap recording that belongs to an archived session (started during it), placed on the session's clock; refuses while a live session owns the strap; a downloaded recording dated outside the session (or undated) is handed to the rescue backup instead.

branches.effect: storedIsThisSession = policy says it belongs to this session AND it began <= end; nil date → false

branches.cond: no live session owns the strap AND (strap is recording OR stored exercise is this session's)
branches.effect: proceeds to download; otherwise logs and returns []

branches.cond: downloaded recording has a start date <= session end
branches.effect: returns its points on the session clock; otherwise (nil start or later start) rescues it via onUnrecoveredDataRescued and returns []

flags.text: Whether a still-running strap recording can be pulled depends on which writer last set collector.isCollecting: the binding sets it to isRecordingOnDevice, which makes strapRecordingBelongsToLiveSession true and refuses the pull, while a later morning/stream stop resets it to false and allows it.

units.does: Writes the merged RR series and a new DataSourceSummary (selector's normalized source or 'internal', streamed/device/total beats, kept reconnectCount and deviceModel) into the archived session before re-analysis.
Appends a session id to the UserDefaults list of reviewed recovered workouts (dedup, keep last 50).
At launch, surfaces the review/trim card for the newest archived workout from the last 48 h that carries a partialDataReason and has not been reviewed; no-op if a card is already showing.

branches.cond: a review card is already set
for each candidate workout entry, newest first
entry id is in the reviewed set

branches.effect: sets card and breaks; otherwise continue

units.does: Resolves the interrupted workout to recover: the persisted crash flag if it is a non-live, un-archived workout; else (off-main) the newest un-archived, un-deleted workout backup indexed and captured in the last 24 h that is not live.

branches.cond: persisted state exists, is a workout, not live, and not archived
branches.effect: returns its id; otherwise scans backups in a detached task

units.does: Manual 'Recover workout from strap' card: finds the interrupted workout, rebuilds it via recoverWorkoutFromBackup (strap-first), and clears the crash flag if it named that session.

branches.effect: clears the persisted flag if it names this id; nil leaves it

units.does: Clears the persisted recording state only when it names the given session id.

Launch auto-recovery of a crashed workout: finds it, counts the attempt (max 3), registers it as running, requires the strap reachable and still recording, bails if a different recording has since started, then rebuilds via recoverWorkoutFromBackup and on success clears the flag and attempt counter.

branches.cond: strap not reachable or not recording on device
branches.effect: logs and returns (flag left for manual card); attempt already counted

branches.cond: persisted state now names a different session

branches.effect: returns leaving flag and counter; otherwise clears both

flags.text: The attempt is counted before the strap check, so three launches without the strap in range permanently disable auto-recovery for that workout; the counter is documented as a guard against memory-kill relaunch loops only.

InterruptedWorkoutAutoRecovery.begin runs only after the awaited detached backup scan and attempt bookkeeping; AppLaunchRecovery.savedByAutoRecovery calls waitUntilDone, which returns immediately while the id is not yet registered, so the launch alert can rebuild the same workout alongside auto-recovery.

It requires the strap to still be recording (line 549) and then calls recoverWorkoutFromBackup, whose strap pull refuses because that same recording sets collector.isCollecting (strapRecordingBelongsToLiveSession); it archives the disk-only workout and logs 'merged strap + streamed'.

units.does: Begins a transfer, reconnects, refreshes the strap's recording status within the feature-ready window and returns whether it is still recording on device.

Launch recovery of an interrupted overnight into a resumable paused state: SessionRecoveryService rebuilds/analyses from backup and archives it paused; then the collector enters paused state, the paused-session marker is persisted and the recording marker cleared.

branches.cond: service returned nil (no backup or archive failed)

units.does: Main-actor: publishes a recovered paused session as current and paused (beat count, isPaused, phase .paused, needsAcceptance false) and bumps the archive signal.
Pure: rebuilds a child night's beats appended to the parent's, shifted by max(parent duration, wall-clock gap between starts); for v5-corrupted children only the tail after parentBeatCount is taken.

branches.effect: takes childSeries.points.suffix(from: parentBeatCount); otherwise all child points

branches.cond: parent last point endMs/t_ms nil (empty parent)

units.does: One-time migration body: walks linked overnight sessions, repairing each whose merge was lost; bumps the archive signal if any repaired; returns the count.

flags.text: The only caller starts this in a Task.detached whose handle is discarded (RRCollector+Bindings.swift:391), so nothing cancels it and the Task.isCancelled branch never runs; the doc's 'aborts the migration on app termination or a shutdown signal' is not implemented.

units.does: Reads archive entries on the main actor and returns the overnight ones with a non-empty linkedSessionIds.
Loads a linked child and its first parent, computes MergeDamage, builds repaired points and rebuilds/archives; returns whether a repair was written.

branches.cond: entry has no first linked id
child or parent fails to load, or either has an empty/nil rrSeries

units.does: True when any of needsMerge, isV5Corrupted, summaryStale, startDateWrong is set.

Pure: classifies a linked child: needsMerge when child beats <= parent beats, v5 corruption via SessionRecoveryMath, summaryStale when dataSourceSummary.totalBeats != child beats, startDateWrong when child start is >30 min after parent start.
Pure: repaired beat series — merged parent+child (mergedRepairPoints) when a merge or v5 fix is needed, else the child as-is; nil if the result exceeds 2x(parent+child) beats or 200,000 beats.

branches.effect: merges; otherwise keeps child points (re-analysis only)
returns it; otherwise logs and returns nil

units.does: Rebuilds the repaired overnight through the morning pipeline (anchored to the parent's start, background-refinement mode), carries user edits over, then archives and re-uploads.

flags.text: A child with nil endDate is rebuilt ending at the migration's run time, which can be days after the night, stretching the session duration used for sleep/window selection.

units.does: Copies tags, notes, sleepUserAdjusted and (when the rebuild has none) vitalsSnapshot from the old session to the repaired one.

branches.cond: repaired has no vitalsSnapshot and old has one
branches.effect: copies old vitals; otherwise keeps repaired's

units.does: Archives the repaired session on the main actor and fires a force re-upload to iCloud; returns success.
File-scope: backup ids indexed since cutoff that are neither archived nor deleted and are still flagged un-archived in RawRRBackup.
File-scope: among candidate ids, the newest backup that decodes, was captured since cutoff and has a WorkoutTrackBackup; nil if none.
File-scope main-actor: reads the per-session auto-recovery attempt count; under 3 increments it and returns true, otherwise logs and returns false.

flags.text: Per-session keys 'autoRecoverAttempts_<uuid>' are removed only on successful recovery, so failed sessions leave keys in standard UserDefaults indefinitely.

units.does: Inserts a session id into the locked running set.
Removes a session id from the locked running set.
Returns whether the id is in the locked running set.
Polls isRunning every 0.5 s until the id is no longer running or `limit` (default 150 s) passes.

branches.cond: id still running and deadline not reached
branches.effect: sleeps 0.5 s and re-checks; otherwise returns (also immediately if never registered)
